claims.text: The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles have a homogenized elemental distribution.
Cu is the lower-melting-point element relevant to melting initiation in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Heating causes Cu atoms to diffuse toward and segregate at the nanoparticle surface.
Cu surface segregation initiates the onset of melting.
Cu enrichment at the nanoparticle surface locally lowers the melting temperature.
The locally reduced surface melting temperature produces a premelt liquid layer.
The premelt liquid layer drives the overall phase transition as temperature rises.
The premelt liquid layer propagates inward with increasing temperature.
A Cu-enriched, liquid-like surface layer will appear before complete nanoparticle melting.
The heated particles will exhibit morphological changes in TEM associated with the early liquid-like surface layer.
Baseline homogeneous nanoparticles exhibit no significant surface composition gradient.
Baseline homogeneous nanoparticles exhibit a sharp melting event at a higher, spatially uniform melting temperature.
The premelting effect is significant only within a temperature interval immediately below complete melting.
The effect on melting behavior is minimal at temperatures substantially below or above the premelting interval.
Particle size and experimental conditions may influence the onset temperature of segregation and its impact on melting progression.
